title: To amend the Federal Election Campaign Act to extend through 2018 the authority of the Federal Election Commission to impose civil money penalties on the basis of a schedule of penalties established and published by the Commission, to expand such authority to certain other violations, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Amends the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971 to extend through December 31, 2018, the authority of the Federal Election Commission (FEC) to impose civil money penalties on the basis of a schedule of penalties it has established and published.

Applies such penalties to violations of qualified campaign contribution and expenditure disclosure requirements.

summary.headline: A 2013 law extended the Federal Election Commission's power to fine people for certain campaign disclosure violations through the end of 2018.
summary.what_it_does: The law extends the Federal Election Commission's authority to impose civil money penalties through December 31, 2018. The penalties follow a schedule of fines that the Commission sets and publishes. The law also applies these penalties to violations of certain campaign contribution and expenditure disclosure rules.

who_it_affects.group: Federal election campaigns and political committees
who_it_affects.how: Those that fail to meet the covered contribution and expenditure disclosure requirements can face fines set by the Commission's published schedule.
The agency keeps its authority to assess these fixed-schedule civil penalties until the end of 2018.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on December 26, 2013, and the penalty authority it extends runs through December 31, 2018.
